caseno: Death Reference Case No 12 of 2005 with Criminal Appeal Nos. 584, 614, with Jail Appeal Nos. 152 and 153.

Md Shafiqul Alam, Assistant Attorney-General—For the State Appellant. 
Abdul Malek, with SM Shahjahan and AM Aminuddin, Advocates—For the Appellant in Criminal Appeal No. 614 of 2005. 
Khondker Mahbub Hossain, with Md Masudul Haque, Advocates—For the Appellant in Criminal Appeal No. 584 of 2005.

full_judgment: 11. Mr SM Shahjahan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of Mr Abdul Malek and Mr AM Amin Uddin, the learned Advocates, for Anwar Hossain, the appellant in Criminal Appeal No. 614 of 2005, makes his submission assailing the impugned judgment and order, opposing the reference and supporting the appeal. He submits that the story of calling and taking away the deceased by this appellant and accused Abu Bakar has not been proved as there are glaring inconsistencies and contradictions in the evidence of PWs 1, 7 and 10 in that regard. Moreover, alleged fact of calling and taking away the deceased long before his death is not conclusive proof of the involvement of this appellant in shooting the deceased to death. In this regard he refers the cases of Shamsuddin vs State 11 DLR (SC) 365 and State vs Khasru Syed Mostafa Hossain 43 DLR (AD) 182. He further submits that there are glaring inconsistencies and contradictions in the evidence of PWs 2, 3, 4, 6 and 9 as to their witnessing the occurrence of , shooting the deceased to death Moreover, presence of PWs 2, 4 and 9 at the material time in the place of occurrence has not been supported by the PWs 3 and 6. Furthermore, there was unexplained inordinate delay in recording the statements under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure of PWs 2, 4, 5 and 9 and for that their evidence should be left out of consideration. The evidence of PWs 3 and 6 as to witnessing the occurrence is inconsistent with their respective statements under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and also with the first information report. Moreover, those alleged eye-witnesses did not give any means of witnessing the occurrence and recognition of the accused persons. So, the evidence of those witnesses suffers from infirmity. Furthermore, none of the employees or guards of the factory was examined. They were withheld without explanation. As such, presumption would be that had they been examined they would not have supported the prosecution case. The evidence of PW 5 that he saw the accused persons running away from the place of occurrence after firing is not credible as it is in the first information report as well as in the evidence that PW 5 accompanied PW 1 M the place of occurrence long after the occurrence. The learned Advocate further submits that PW 1 immediately after the occurrence over telephone informed Shyampur Police Station the fact of commission of the offence of murder. Such information was recorded in GD Entry No. 725 dated 9-11-1999, which is the first information report within the meaning of section 154 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. None was named as accused in that GD Entry. Moreover, the GD Entry was suppressed. On the basis of that GD entry PW 14 rushed to the place of occurrence and started investigation of the case making inquest of the dead body of the deceased in presence of informant PW 1 and his son PWs 6 and others, sent the dead body to the morgue for post mortem examination and seized the alamats from the place of occurrence under a seizure list, of which PWs 1 and 6 are the witnesses At that time the informant PW 1 and PW 6 did not disclose to PW 14 the names of the assailants. So none was named as the assailants in the inquest report. Due to non-disclosure of the names of the convicts as the assailants at that time casts serious doubt as to their involvement in the occurrence. In this regard the learned Counsel refers the cases of State vs Paran Chandra Baroi, 2 BCR 292 and 1986 BCR (AD) 225. He also submits that the FIR recorded during investigation of the case is not an FIR in the eye of law, but a statement under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Thus, the prosecution could not prove involvement of appellant Anwar in commission of the offence. The learned Judge of the Tribunal committed error in convicting and sentencing him. With these few words he canvasses for rejection of the reference and acquittal of appellant Anwar.
